contentHtml:
UAE— SAKINA, the mental health network operated by SEHA, will host its inaugural SAKINA for Children Education Summit (SCES 2026) at Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers to strengthen collaboration between healthcare professionals, educators and families in supporting children’s mental health.

The summit will take place under the patronage of Sheikha Hamda bint Khalifa Al Nahyan, SAKINA Ambassador for Strategic Initiatives.

 It will focus on improving early identification of mental health concerns, expanding access to timely interventions and ensuring continuity of care as children progress into adulthood.

Held under the theme, “From Early Years to Emerging Adults: Supporting Resilience Across the Developmental Journey”, the event will examine how mental health needs change from early childhood through adolescence and young adulthood.

Bridging healthcare and education

The scientific programme will cover early childhood development, student wellbeing, child and adolescent mental health, and clinical and therapeutic approaches.

Expert-led sessions and multidisciplinary discussions will explore evidence-based ways to strengthen early intervention, build resilience and improve coordination between healthcare providers, schools and community services.

The discussions will also address how families, educators and healthcare professionals can recognise early signs of mental health concerns and guide children towards appropriate support.

This approach reflects growing recognition of the need to integrate mental health services into education and community settings rather than relying solely on clinical interventions.

Sheikha Hamda bint Khalifa Al Nahyan said children’s mental health was a shared responsibility involving families, schools and communities.

She noted that stronger collaboration, greater awareness and earlier support could help create environments in which young people develop confidence and resilience.

She also highlighted the importance of investing in children’s mental wellbeing to support healthier families and communities across the UAE.

Strengthening multidisciplinary mental healthcare

Dr Zain Ali Al Yafei, Chief Executive Officer of SAKINA, said addressing the mental health needs of children and young people required coordinated action across prevention, early identification, specialist treatment and ongoing support.

He explained that the summit would provide a platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration among healthcare, government and education stakeholders.

The initiative also seeks to improve pathways between identifying mental health concerns and accessing appropriate care.

According to Al Yafei, SAKINA aims to develop an integrated and sustainable mental health system that supports younger generations and strengthens long-term community wellbeing.

The summit builds on the network’s work in mental healthcare, particularly in prevention, access to services and rehabilitation.

By bringing together professionals working with children and adolescents, the event will provide opportunities to share clinical knowledge, discuss emerging challenges and improve coordination across sectors.

SAKINA has invited healthcare professionals, educators, researchers and other stakeholders involved in child and adolescent mental health to participate in the inaugural summit.
